skill.name: attribution-reconciler
skill.description: Reconciles paid advertising conversion exports against GA4 or ecommerce order IDs. It de-duplicates stacked platform credit, normalizes attribution windows and currency, compares attribution models, and reads incrementality from holdout tests.
skill.summary: Reconcile paid ad attribution against order IDs.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

The phrase asks the assistant to find double-counted paid conversions in supplied marketing exports. It is not system reconnaissance or host environment discovery.

content.value_statement: Ad platforms often claim the same sale, which makes conversion totals unreliable. This skill reconciles platform exports against order IDs, normalizes windows and currency, and separates real orders from stacked credit.
actual_capabilities: Uses GA4 or ecommerce order IDs as the paid conversion truth set.
Matches platform-reported conversions to real orders by order ID or fallback fields.
Separates matched, double-counted, and unmatched conversion claims.
Normalizes attribution windows and currencies before comparing platforms.
Compares at least two attribution models on the same de-duped orders.
Reads geo or holdout incrementality when test and control exports exist.
limitations: Requires a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export before reconciliation can start.
Does not compute ROAS, CPA, ROI, or EMV ratios.
Does not infer incrementality without geo or holdout test data.
Covers paid channels, not organic dark-social attribution or GA4 direct decomposition.

use_cases.title: Monthly Paid Media Close
use_cases.description: Reconcile Meta and Google conversion exports against ecommerce order IDs before reporting month-end paid results.

use_cases.title: Analytics Data Quality Review
use_cases.description: Find unmatched claims, duplicated order IDs, and window differences before building attribution dashboards.

use_cases.title: Holdout Test Readout
use_cases.description: Compare platform-attributed conversions with geo holdout lift when test and control exports are available.

prompt_templates.title: Start Monthly Reconciliation
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile my paid conversions for [month]. Use this GA4 order-ID export as the truth set. Compare it with these Meta and Google conversion exports.

prompt_templates.title: Normalize Windows And Currency
prompt_templates.prompt: Build the attribution workbook. Normalize Meta [window], Google [window], and all currencies to [currency], then match each platform claim to the order-ID export.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Credit Models
prompt_templates.prompt: After de-duplicating real orders, compare last-click and linear attribution. Show how credit changes without changing the real conversion count.

prompt_templates.title: Read Holdout Incrementality
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced geo or holdout test readout.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these test-region and control-region order exports with platform spend. Read incrementality, compare it with last-click claims, and prepare a handoff summary.

output_examples.input: A GA4 order export and Meta plus Google conversion exports for May.
output: A match table showing matched, double-counted, and unmatched platform claims.
A de-duped conversion count by platform using order IDs as the truth set.
A short handoff summary for downstream ROAS calculation.

output_examples.input: Platform exports with different attribution windows and currencies.
output: A normalized-window view that places each claim on the same comparison basis.
A currency-normalized value table with the rate stated clearly.
A note explaining which counts are ready for ratio analysis.

output_examples.input: A geo holdout export with test and control region orders.
output: An incrementality read for the holdout period.
A comparison between observed lift and last-click platform claims.
An N/A marker if the holdout data is incomplete.

best_practices: Provide order IDs, timestamps, value, and currency for the truth-set export.
State each platform attribution window before asking for a match table.
Use holdout data for incrementality instead of inferring lift from attribution alone.
anti_patterns: Do not reconcile against platform conversion totals without an order-ID truth set.
Do not compare platforms before windows and currencies are normalized.
Do not treat duplicated platform credit as multiple real orders.

faq.question: What data do I need to start?
faq.answer: You need a GA4 or ecommerce order-ID export and each paid platform conversion export.

faq.question: Does this skill connect directly to ad APIs?
faq.answer: No. It works from user-provided exports. Optional connectors may help collect the same owned data.

faq.question: Can it compute ROAS or CPA?
faq.answer: No. It prepares clean de-duped counts for a separate ROI or ROAS calculator.

faq.question: How does it handle Meta and Google double-counting?
faq.answer: It matches both claims to the same order ID and counts the order once in the truth set.

faq.question: Can it measure incrementality?
faq.answer: Yes, when a geo or holdout export provides test and control data for the period.

faq.question: Will it save results automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the assistant to ask before writing a workbook or memory notes.
